searchText: gm, was wondering what you guys think of ZK rollups vs ORs, i feel like ORs gonna win ZKRs, cuz it's advantage outweighs ZKR's ORs advantages: * has EVM, you don' t have to write in Cario ZKRs advantages: * Faster withrawal periods (might be solved on ORs by ZK checkpoints on ORs) * less data on chain, lower fees (most of this data only has to live temporarily post sharding) thoughts? where am I wrong? How can I get added to speak in <#745077610685661265> ? Had a comment on transient storage discussion <@533350294059352074> - you should be good now! Thanks Tim! zksync will have evm although I think some opcodes aren't fully compatible starknet isn't the only zkrollup there are several coming i feel like ORs will win here ors are worse in everything but how easy they are to write (well, also execution cost, but is that really significant per tx?) what are they worse at except txn costs and withdrawal times? trust? Also, I would say txn costs (or linear vs logarithmic scalability) is kind of a biggy, as that's like the whole purpose of this rollup thing no? 1 zkrollups only need to post state deltas, orus need to post everything, which means theoretically (as far as on-chain data goes) zkrollups allow for infinite tps. 2 they also allow maximum compression because decompression doesn't have to be possible on-chain at all - unlike orus 3 security is crypto based rather than fraud proof based, so nobody needs to watch for correctness. how many people *actually* are going to watch for fake state attempts on orus? major orus probably will have someone, but a small fork - not necessarily. a small fork of eg. zksync will still be safe last but not least, zkrollups allow native anonymity/privacy, while orus don't. this is starting to go beyond evm. but it would be possible to have almost-compatible evm zkrollups in which all eoas are fully anon how does it logarithmicly scale? why is it more trust worthy? 1 - i think ORs only have to post state merkle roots 2 - eh, the compression is just for the temp data you put on chain that is gonna be deleted 3 - you only have to have 1 player that watches for correctness, talking about a big OR 4 - the proover will see your txn i think, you might be able to slide in an anon one, but thats not the main usecase, and i don't think people care about privacy that much rn I'm in no way an expert, but I don't understand point 3? How do you only need 1 player? The more the better AFAIK, or are you willing to trust only one node to submit fraud proofs? As far as people not caring about privacy, I don't know about that one chief. I know I do. Again, I am no expert, but I fail to see how ZK rollups are not superior to Optimistic rollups. The only thing I can see is that ORs are further along in development/adoption.

excerpts.author: 0xsadcat
excerpts.content:
1 zkrollups only need to post state deltas, orus need to post everything, which means theoretically (as far as on-chain data goes) zkrollups allow for infinite tps.
2 they also allow maximum compression because decompression doesn't have to be possible on-chain at all - unlike orus
3 security is crypto based rather than fraud proof based, so nobody needs to watch for correctness. how many people *actually* are going to watch for fake state attempts on orus? major orus probably will have someone, but a small fork - not necessarily. a small fork of eg. zksync will still be safe

last but not least, zkrollups allow native anonymity/privacy, while orus don't. this is starting to go beyond evm. but it would be possible to have almost-compatible evm zkrollups in which all eoas are fully anon
